items.claim: Each geometry has diagram, Aut/Cor groups, Borel, action kernels, truncation and doubling links supplied in the cited complete supplement.
Two rank2 and ten rank3 geometries are higher-rank truncations; nontruncation rank1,2,3,4,5,6,>=7 counts0,4,20,41,8,1,0.
Eight sporadic groups: orders, subgroup conjugacy-class counts, subgroup totals and nontruncation geometry counts at ranks2–6. Not the all-geometries convention of L096.
No geometry of rank at least7 in the eight reported sporadic classifications; all relevant geometries asserted known.
Hoffman–Singleton graph has50 vertices,175 edges, full flag-transitive U3(5):2; such a maximal subgroup occurs in HS.
Each quadric contains50 points and each point lies on50 quadrics.
Each conic contains8 points and lies on8 quadrics.
Two conics through any point pair; each common quadric contains at least one; exactly two quadrics contain both conics.
A conic gives a point/quadric bijection satisfying the two displayed incidence implications.
HS acts transitively on conics and incident/nonincident point–quadric pairs and doubly transitively on points/quadrics; conic stabilizerS8.
PointsP, lines all point pairs, planes conics; symmetric containment gives HoSi.c* rank3 geometry; residues HoSi/K8/digon; type sizes176/15400/1100, Aut=HS and BorelS6; explicit supplement name3.2.
Replace conic planes by176 quadrics; a line is incident to a plane exactly when plane contains line and both conics through it. Both end residues HoSi; middle digon; Aut=HS, Cor=Aut(HS), BorelS6.
All16 references read; earlier classifications and source algorithms distinguished from proofs supplied in this six-page article.
